en: to be stopped; to be suspended

examples.en: The elevator suddenly stopped.

examples.ko: 비밀번호를 세 번 틀리면 계정이 정지돼요.
examples.en: If you get the password wrong three times, the account is suspended.
I captured the frozen screen.

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 오전에는 공장 기계가 정지될 거예요.
examples.en: The factory machines will be stopped in the morning because of the construction.
When the car stopped, people got off.
My driver's license was suspended, so I can't drive.

explain: '멈추다'와 달리 '정지되다'는 기계, 계정, 면허처럼 '누가 멈추게 한' 것에 주로 써요. 사람이 걷다가 멈출 때는 '멈추다', '서다'를 써요. 기계·서비스의 '일시 정지'는 '일시 정지돼요'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Train service was suspended because of the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스나 기차가 다니지 않을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when buses or trains stop running.

phrases.en: The elevator is stopped right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이지 않는 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a state where something does not move.

phrases.en: The clock suddenly stopped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler and broader word for everyday talk.

explain_en: Unlike 멈추다, 정지되다 mostly describes machines, accounts or licenses that were stopped by something. For a person stopping while walking, use 멈추다 or 서다. For machines and services, '일시 정지되다' means 'temporarily suspended'.

en: to vent one's anger on; to take out on

examples.en: Please do not take your anger out on me.
He took out his anger by throwing things.

examples.ko: 스트레스 받는다고 가족에게 화풀이하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take your stress out on your family.
Some of my friends vent their anger through exercise.
If I am upset, I will go to karaoke and blow off steam.
Why are you taking it out on me?

explain: '~에게/한테 화풀이하다'처럼 대상을 말해요. 그 사람이 화난 이유가 아닌데 터뜨린다는 느낌이에요. '화를 풀다'는 마음을 가라앉힌다는 좋은 뜻도 되지만, '화풀이하다'는 남에게 터뜨리는 나쁜 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 기분이 나빠도 남에게 화풀이하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Even if you feel bad, you shouldn't take it out on others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에게'로 화를 받는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 에게 marks the person who receives the anger.
phrases.en_equiv: to take it out on others

phrases.example: 너무 화가 나서 누구에게든 화풀이하고 싶었어요.
phrases.en: I was so angry that I wanted to take it out on anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 싶다 expresses the feeling.
phrases.en_equiv: to want to vent one's anger

phrases.en: I regretted taking my anger out on my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아서/어서'로 이유와 결과를 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: -아서/어서 links the cause and the result.

explain_en: The target takes '~에게/한테': '~에게 화풀이하다'. It implies the person is not the reason for the anger. '화를 풀다' can mean calming down in a good way, but '화풀이하다' is negative, letting it out on others.

en: to have a crick; to feel a stitch

examples.en: I overdid my workout yesterday, so I have a stitch in my side.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘못 잤는지 목이 결려서 고개를 못 돌려요.
examples.en: I must have slept wrong; my neck is stiff and I can't turn my head.

examples.ko: 숨을 크게 쉬면 가슴이 결리는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: When I breathe deeply, my chest feels like it catches.
After sitting for a long time, my back got a crick.
When your lower back is cricked, apply a warm compress.
Even though my shoulder hurts, I can't be bothered to go to the hospital.

explain: '아프다'와 달리 숨을 쉬거나 움직일 때 걸리는 듯 찌릿한 느낌에 써요. 아픈 부위가 주어라서 '옆구리가 결리다', '어깨가 결리다'처럼 말해요. 비슷하게 '담이 걸리다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My shoulder feels stiff and catchy after using the computer for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 부위를 바꿔 '허리가', '등이'처럼 다양하게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can swap in other body parts, like 허리가 or 등이.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a crick in the shoulder

phrases.en: I woke up with a crick in my neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결리다'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 근육이 뭉쳐서 움직이기 힘들 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 결리다, used when a muscle seizes up and is hard to move.

phrases.en: I put a patch on the spot that hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여서 아픈 곳을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 lets you describe the aching spot.

explain_en: Unlike plain '아프다', it describes a catching, twinging feeling when you breathe or move. The sore body part is the subject, as in '옆구리가 결리다' or '어깨가 결리다'. People also say '담이 걸리다' for a similar feeling.

examples.en: I always wear rubber gloves when doing dishes.
The rubber gloves tore, so I bought new ones.
My hands got rough, so I clean wearing rubber gloves.
Water got inside the rubber gloves.
Mom, where are the rubber gloves?
I made kimchi wearing red rubber gloves.

explain: '장갑을 끼다/벗다'처럼 '끼다'와 함께 써요. 설거지나 청소, 김장할 때 쓰는 두꺼운 장갑이라서 얇은 '비닐장갑'과 구분해요.

phrases.en: I wear rubber gloves when I clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장갑은 '끼다'와 함께 쓰는 것이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gloves naturally go with 끼다.

phrases.en: I finished the dishes and took off the rubber gloves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끼는 것의 반대 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of putting them on.

phrases.en: I bought a pair of rubber gloves at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장갑은 두 짝이 한 쌍이라 '켤레'로 세어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gloves come as a pair, so they are counted with 켤레.

explain_en: Use it with '끼다' and '벗다', as in '장갑을 끼다'. It is a thick glove for dishes, cleaning and kimchi making, so it is distinguished from thin '비닐장갑'.

examples.en: The smell is so bad that I feel nauseous.
I rode in the car for a long time and now I feel nauseous.

examples.ko: 그 장면을 보고 구역질이 날 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I felt like gagging when I saw that scene.
I opened the window to hold back the nausea.

examples.ko: 이틀 전부터 구역질이 나고 입맛이 없어요.
examples.en: Since two days ago, I've felt nauseous and have had no appetite.
After taking the medicine, the nausea stopped.

explain: 토할 것처럼 속이 울렁거리고 헛구역질이 나는 느낌이에요. 실제로 토하는 건 '토하다'이고, '속이 안 좋다'나 '메스껍다'는 더 부드러운 말이에요. 아주 싫은 것을 보았을 때도 '구역질이 나다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: It was so spicy that I gagged.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구역질이 나다'는 느낌이고, '구역질을 하다'는 실제로 헛구역질을 하는 행동이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 구역질이 나다 is the feeling; 구역질을 하다 is the actual act of retching.

phrases.en: There is a nauseating smell from the trash can.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새나 장면이 아주 싫을 때 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a noun after it for a smell or sight that is really disgusting.

phrases.en: My stomach feels queasy on the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구역질보다 부드럽고 일상에서 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday way to say you feel sick.

explain_en: Everyday word for the retching reaction or gagging (구역질이 나다) It is the feeling of your stomach heaving as if you will vomit. Actually throwing up is '토하다', while '속이 안 좋다' and '메스껍다' are softer. People also say '구역질이 나다' when they find something disgusting.

t90.ax: The smell is so bad that I feel nauseous.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 근시라서 안경을 써요.
examples.en: I have been nearsighted since I was little, so I wear glasses.
If you look at a smartphone for a long time, nearsightedness gets worse.
I had a nearsightedness test at the eye clinic.

examples.ko: 근시인 사람은 멀리 있는 글씨가 흐리게 보여요.
examples.en: For nearsighted people, far-away letters look blurry.
I heard nearsightedness in children is increasing every year.

examples.ko: 약한 근시는 렌즈로 쉽게 교정할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Mild nearsightedness is easy to correct with lenses.

explain: '근시'는 가까운 것은 잘 보이고 먼 것은 흐리게 보이는 눈이에요. 반대로 먼 것은 보이고 가까운 것이 흐린 눈은 '원시'라고 해요. 보통 '근시예요', '근시라서 안경을 써요'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: My nearsightedness is severe, so I'm uncomfortable without glasses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 많이 나쁠 때 '심하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with '심하다' when the eyesight is very bad.

phrases.en: I got new glasses for nearsightedness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼 곳이 잘 보이도록 만든 안경을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means glasses made so that you can see far away clearly.

phrases.example: 저는 근시가 아니라서 안경을 안 써요.
phrases.en: I'm not nearsighted, so I don't wear glasses.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근시예요'의 부정형으로, 눈이 나쁘지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the negative of '근시예요', used to say your eyes are not bad.

explain_en: 근시 is an eye condition where near things look clear and far things look blurry. The opposite, where far things are clear and near ones are blurry, is 원시. People usually say 근시예요 or 근시라서 안경을 써요.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 아이들 배 속에 기생충이 많았어요.
examples.en: In the past, many children had parasites in their stomachs.

examples.ko: 생선을 날로 먹으면 기생충에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat raw fish, you can get parasites.

examples.ko: 기생충 약을 먹고 병원에서 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: I took anti-parasite medicine and got a test at the hospital.
Puppies also need a parasite check.

examples.ko: 어떤 기생충은 다른 동물의 몸에서 살아요.
examples.en: Some parasites live inside another animal's body.
I watched the film 'Parasite' at a movie theater.

explain: 몸 안팎에 붙어서 사는 벌레를 말해요. 사람에게 '기생충 같다'고 하면 남에게 기대어 사는 사람을 심하게 낮추는 말이니 조심해야 해요. 영화 「기생충」 덕분에 외국 사람에게도 익숙한 단어가 됐어요.

phrases.en: We had a parasite test at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸속에 기생충이 있는지 확인하는 검사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A test to check whether there are parasites in the body.

phrases.example: 손을 안 씻으면 기생충이 생길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you don't wash your hands, you can get parasites.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 기생충이 들어와 살게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when parasites get into the body and begin to live there.

phrases.en: I took medicine and got rid of the parasites.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료해서 기생충을 몸에서 없앨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when treatment removes parasites from the body.

explain_en: It means worms and creatures that live on or inside a body. Calling a person '기생충 같다' insults someone who lives off others, so be careful. The film 'Parasite' made the word familiar to foreigners.

en: to be haggard; to be emaciated

examples.en: My younger brother is a bit prickly today.
My skin was dry and rough because I couldn't sleep.
He's a prickly person, so it's hard to talk to him.
Everyone will get irritable during exam period.
When my friend is hungry, he gets snippy and curt.
The team leader was sharp in the meeting, so I got nervous.

explain: 사람에게 쓰면 '예민하고 말이 날카롭다'는 느낌이고, 피부나 수염에 쓰면 '거칠고 윤기가 없다'는 뜻이에요. 살이 빠져 수척해 보이는 얼굴에도 써요. '화나다'처럼 한순간의 감정이 아니라 계속되는 태도에 가까워요. '까칠남', '까칠녀'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: That person has a bit of a prickly personality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예민하고 말이 날카로운 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a sensitive, sharp-tongued personality.

phrases.en: My face looks haggard because I haven't slept for days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피곤하고 수척해 보이는 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a face that looks tired and worn.

phrases.en: Why are you talking so sharply?
phrases.nuance_ko: 부드럽지 않고 날카롭게 말하는 태도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking in a sharp, unfriendly way.

explain_en: Tired, dry-looking skin or face, also cranky — casual, spoken. For people, 까칠하다 means sharp, touchy, and hard to please; for skin or stubble it means rough and lacking moisture. It can also describe a thin, worn-out face. Unlike 화나다, it is a lasting attitude rather than a momentary feeling. It also appears as 까칠남 and 까칠녀.

t90.ax: My younger brother is a bit prickly today.

examples.en: I fell on the icy road and hurt my tailbone.

examples.ko: 꼬리뼈가 아파서 오래 앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My tailbone hurts, so it's hard to sit for long.

examples.ko: 의자에 앉을 때 꼬리뼈가 눌려서 쿠션을 깔았어요.
examples.en: My tailbone got pressed when I sat, so I put a cushion down.
I landed hard on my bottom, and now my tailbone throbs.

examples.ko: 병원에서 꼬리뼈 사진을 찍어 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: At the hospital they said let's take an X-ray of the tailbone.
Humans have a tailbone, but no tail.

explain: 넘어져서 엉덩이를 세게 다쳤을 때 '꼬리뼈가 아프다'라고 구체적으로 말해요. 병원에서도 이렇게 설명하면 잘 통해요.

phrases.en: My tailbone hurts a lot since I fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 뒤의 아픈 증상을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to describe pain after an injury.

phrases.en: I got a bruise around my tailbone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부분'을 붙여서 아픈 곳의 위치를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '부분' lets you point out where the problem is.

phrases.en: I went to the hospital because of tailbone pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 증상을 설명할 때 쓰는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more formal phrase, useful for describing symptoms at a clinic.

explain_en: When you fall and hurt your bottom, people say specifically '꼬리뼈가 아프다'. Describing it this way also works well at a hospital.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 에어컨 바람을 쐬었더니 냉방병에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: After being in the air conditioning all day, I came down with air-conditioning sickness.

examples.ko: 냉방병 때문에 머리가 아프고 몸이 으슬으슬해요.
examples.en: Because of air-conditioning sickness, I have a headache and the chills.
Lots of people get air-conditioning sickness in the office.

examples.ko: 냉방병을 막으려면 실내 온도를 너무 낮추지 마세요.
examples.en: To prevent air-conditioning sickness, don't set the room temperature too low.

examples.ko: 여름 감기가 사실은 냉방병일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: What seems like a summer cold could actually be air-conditioning sickness.

examples.ko: 냉방병에 걸리지 않게 얇은 겉옷을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I brought a thin jacket so I wouldn't get air-conditioning sickness.

explain: 더운 바깥과 시원한 실내의 온도 차이 때문에 감기처럼 몸이 안 좋을 때 써요. 보통 '냉방병에 걸리다'라고 말해요. 여름에 자주 듣는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 에어컨 앞에 오래 앉아 있다가 냉방병에 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: I sat in front of the air conditioner too long and got AC sickness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸렸다고 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to say someone caught this illness.

phrases.example: 두통과 피로는 냉방병 증상일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Headaches and tiredness can be symptoms of AC sickness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 몸 상태가 나타나는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain what physical signs appear.

phrases.example: 겉옷을 입으면 냉방병을 예방할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Wearing a jacket can help prevent AC sickness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 정보나 조언에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in health tips and advice.

explain_en: It refers to feeling unwell, like a cold, because of the temperature gap between the hot outdoors and the cool indoors. People usually say '냉방병에 걸리다'. It is a word you hear a lot in summer.

en: to patch; to attach an extra piece on top

examples.ko: 무릎 구멍 난 곳에 천을 덧댔어요.
examples.en: I patched the hole at the knee with a piece of cloth.
I put plastic over the window to keep out the cold.

examples.ko: 낡은 신발 밑창에 고무를 덧대서 신어요.
examples.en: I add rubber to the sole of my worn-out shoes and wear them.

examples.ko: 상처 위에 거즈를 덧대고 붕대를 감았어요.
examples.en: I laid gauze over the wound and wrapped a bandage.
Please put a wooden splint on the broken leg.
I came to buy cloth to patch jeans with.

explain: 구멍이나 약한 곳 위에 천, 판 같은 것을 한 겹 더 대는 거예요. '덧붙이다'는 말이나 내용을 더할 때 많이 쓰고, '덧대다'는 물건을 겉에 대는 데 써요.

phrases.example: 청바지 무릎에 천을 덧대면 오래 입어요.
phrases.en: If you patch the knees of jeans with cloth, they last longer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 고칠 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing when mending clothes.

phrases.en: I attached a board over the broken part.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉에 한 겹 더 대고 붙이는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes adding and attaching one more layer on the surface.

phrases.example: 여기에 한 겹 더 덧대 주세요.
phrases.en: Please add one more layer here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to make a request.

explain_en: It means laying another layer, such as cloth or a board, over a hole or weak spot. '덧붙이다' is commonly used for adding words or content, while '덧대다' is for putting a physical item on the surface.

t90.ax: I came to buy cloth to patch jeans with.

en: to hiccup; to have the hiccups

examples.en: My younger brother keeps hiccuping.
I hiccuped during class and was embarrassed.
The hiccuping baby was so cute that I watched for a while.
I hiccuped while drinking soda.
I held my breath so I wouldn't hiccup.
If you hiccup while laughing, it's even funnier.

explain: '딸꾹질이 나요'가 더 자주 들려요. '딸꾹질해요'는 지금 계속하고 있는 모습을 말할 때 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I suddenly have the hiccups.
phrases.nuance_ko: '딸꾹질하다'보다 더 자주 들리는, 딸꾹질이 시작된 때의 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 딸꾹질하다 when hiccups start.

phrases.en: The child has been hiccuping since a while ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딸꾹질이 계속되는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes hiccups that are still going on.

phrases.en: I can hear someone hiccuping in the next seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸미는 말로 바꿔서 소리나 사람을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used to describe a sound or a person.

explain_en: 딸꾹질이 나요 is heard more often. 딸꾹질해요 sounds natural when you describe someone who is hiccuping right now.

examples.en: The baby got heat rash on the neck.

examples.ko: 더운 날 땀띠 때문에 너무 가려워요.
examples.en: On hot days, the heat rash makes me very itchy.

examples.ko: 땀띠에는 시원하게 씻고 말려 주는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For heat rash, it's good to wash coolly and dry the skin.

examples.ko: 땀띠 연고를 바르니까 가려운 게 나아졌어요.
examples.en: After I put heat rash ointment on, the itching got better.

examples.ko: 땀띠 가루를 발라 주니 아기가 편안해 보여요.
examples.en: After I put powder on the heat rash, the baby looks comfortable.
They say heat rash forms when sweat pores get blocked.

explain: 더운 여름에 땀이 많이 나서 피부에 작게 돋는 발진이에요. 보통 '땀띠가 나다'라고 말하고, 아기들에게 많아서 '땀띠 가루'도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 여름에는 아기 등에 땀띠가 자주 나요.
phrases.en: In summer, babies often get heat rash on their backs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '땀띠'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 표현으로, 땀띠가 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase with 땀띠, meaning heat rash has appeared.

phrases.example: 아기 목욕 후에 땀띠 가루를 발라 줬어요.
phrases.en: After the baby's bath, I applied heat rash powder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀띠를 막거나 가라앉히려고 피부에 바르는 가루를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the powder applied to skin to prevent or soothe heat rash.

phrases.example: 땀띠 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't sleep at night because of the heat rash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀띠가 이유가 되어 힘들 때 '때문에'를 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '때문에' says that heat rash is the reason for a problem.

explain_en: It is a small skin rash that appears when you sweat a lot in hot summer. People usually say '땀띠가 나다', and since it is common in babies, '땀띠 가루' (heat rash powder) is a good word to know too.

en: to feel muffled; to feel stuffed up (ears)

examples.ko: 비행기가 높이 올라가면 기압이 낮아져서 귀가 먹먹해져요.
examples.en: When a plane climbs high, the air pressure drops and my ears feel blocked.

examples.ko: 건물 안에서 누군가의 울음소리가 새어 나와서 가슴이 먹먹했어요.
examples.en: Someone's crying leaked out from inside the building and my chest felt heavy.
Maybe I have a cold, my ears feel stuffed.

examples.ko: 수영을 하고 나왔더니 귀가 먹먹한데 물이 들어갔나 봐요.
examples.en: My ears feel blocked after swimming. Maybe water got in.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보고 나니 가슴이 먹먹해서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: After the sad movie my chest felt so heavy that I couldn't speak.
When we entered the tunnel, my ears felt blocked.

explain: 귀에 쓰면 물이나 기압 때문에 소리가 잘 안 들리고 막힌 느낌이에요. 가슴에 쓰면 슬픔이나 감동이 가득 차서 말이 잘 안 나오는 느낌이에요. 귀가 막힌 느낌은 '멍멍하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 소리가 잘 안 들려서 귀가 멍멍해요.
phrases.en: I can't hear well, so my ears feel muffled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀가 막힌 느낌은 '먹먹하다'처럼 '멍멍하다'로도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 'meokmeokhada', it describes ears feeling blocked.

phrases.en: My heart felt heavy at the news of the farewell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬픔이나 감동이 가득 차서 말이 안 나오는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a heart so full of sadness or emotion that words won't come.

phrases.en: The heavy feeling lasted a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '먹먹한'으로 바뀌어서 마음 상태를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes 'meokmeokan', describing a state of mind.

explain_en: With ears, it means a blocked, muffled feeling where sounds are hard to hear because of water or pressure. With the chest, it means sadness or emotion fills you so much that words won't come. The blocked-ear feeling can also be called '멍멍하다'.
